title: Twilio SIDs without a token value
summary: Twilio inputs that carry an identifier but no secret value: an Account SID alone, an API key SID alone, and an Account SID beside a TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN assignment whose value is a template placeholder. Values are synthetic.
rationale: Near neighbors of the paired cases: the identifier shapes are the same, the secret component is absent. A policy that flags every AC or SK value over-redacts; a policy that treats the SID as harmless everywhere is not supported either, since no source states the SID is non-sensitive, which is why the basis is recorded as policy.

expectation.rationale: Question: should an identifier-only input be expected to be flagged. Options: expect flagging (identifier treated as secret); expect no flag (no secret component present). Chosen: expect no flag, since the provider documents the secret as the Auth Token or key secret and no page read says the SID is confidential; the Twilio authtoken page marks accountSid 'Not PII'. This is a project decision, not a provider rule, and does not say a SID is harmless in every setting. Would reverse if Twilio states the SID is confidential or a maintainer decides to treat account identifiers as sensitive. Deciding maintainer and a second reviewer: not yet recorded (draft).

sources.supports: accountSid pattern AC + 32 hex, flagged Not PII; no secrecy statement for the SID
secrecy statement covers the Auth Token only

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
